answer: Agents can earn voting weight only by locking a scarce, nontransferable bond for a fixed period, then completing randomly assigned tasks whose outcomes are checked by independent peers. A new identity starts with little weight; splitting into many identities does not multiply influence because each bond is tied to a real deposit, and dishonest reports can forfeit it. An orchard task might compare juniper samples for ferrous traces: faking many reviewers means funding many bonds and risking each one, so the attack becomes costly rather than free.
